questions.stem: What is the most common cause of hypercalcemia in hospitalized patients?
questions.solutionHtml:
Malignancy
  • Malignancy remains to be the most common cause associated with hypercalcemia in hospitalized patient.


Harrison’s Principles of Internal Medicine, 21st Edition, Page No. 357

questions.stem: The blood investigation of a patient is given below. HBsAg - NRAnti-HBs – NRAnti-HBc IgM – NRAnti HBc total - positiveHBeAg - NRAnti-HBe - NRWhat is the probable diagnosis?

options.label: A
options.text: Acute HBV infection in window period

options.label: C
options.text: HBV infection in the remote past, completely recovered

questions.answerText: HBV infection in the remote past, completely recovered
questions.solutionHtml:
HBV infection in the remote past, completely recovered
  • According to the given serological picture the most probable situation is HBV infection in window phase.
  • The presence of Anti-HBc total (indicating past exposure to HBV) along with absence of HBsAg and Anti-HBs suggests a resolved HBV infection. The individual has developed antibodies (Anti-HBc) in response to a past HBV infection, implying recovery and immunity.


Harrison’s Principles of Internal Medicine, 21st Edition, Page No. 2562

questions.stem: Which of the following proteins shows a marked increase in size in nephrotic syndrome on serum electrophoresis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Alpha 2 globulin
  • Due to massive proteinuria, there is hypoalbuminemia with increase in alpha2 globulin due to increased macroglobulin & low gamma globulins.

questions.stem: Transferrin saturation is decreased in which of the following condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
Iron deficiency anemia
  • Transferrin is the transport molecule for iron. Its saturation decreases in iron deficiency anemia as serum iron levels are low.

questions.stem: A 62-year-old woman presents with a hard, irregular, fixed, and non- mobile lump in her breast. Her nipple is retracted, her skin is discolored, and her lymph nodes are enlarged. What does it mean if the tumor is luminal type A?

options.label: A
options.text: ER +/ HER2 neu-, mild to moderate proliferation

questions.answerText: ER +/ HER2 neu-, mild to moderate proliferation
questions.solutionHtml:
ER +/ HER2 neu-, mild to moderate proliferation
  • Luminal A type of breast cancer is ER+ & her2neu negative with low ki67 index. ki67 is the proliferation marker of tumor cells.

questions.stemHtml: These findings are suggestive of which of the following conditions?
questions.solutionHtml:
Acromegaly
  • The given image shows, frontal bossing, prognathous jaw.
  • Acromegaly is characterized by the excessive production of growth hormone (GH), usually due to a pituitary tumor.
  • This excess GH leads to abnormal growth of bones and tissues. Key features include enlarged hands and feet, facial changes (prognathism, enlarged nose, lips, and ears), and in some cases, frontal bossing.
  • Hence the diagnosis is Acromegaly.


Harrison’s Principles of Internal Medicine, 21st Edition, Page No. 2912

questions.stem: A 60-year-old vegetarian presents with fatigue and weakness that have been present for a few months. On physical examination, pallor is noted. Hemoglobin is 9 g/dL and MCV is increased at 110 fL. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Megaloblastic anaemia
  • Vegetarianism, pallor, fatigue, increased red cell volume are features of megaloblastic anaemia caused by deficiency of vitamin B12.
  • The presentation of fatigue, weakness, pallor, and an increased MCV of 110 fL strongly suggests a megaloblastic anemia. This type of anemia is often caused by deficiencies in vitamin B12 or folate, leading to impaired DNA synthesis in red blood cell production, resulting in larger, immature red blood cells (macrocytes).


Harrison’s Principles of Internal Medicine, 21st Edition, Page No. 766

questions.stem: A patient with history of rheumatic heart disease, is now found to have vegetations along the valve leaflets. What is correct about obtaining the blood samples of this patient?

options.label: B
options.text: Collect 3 sets of samples from 3 different sites at the same time

options.label: C
options.text: Collect 3 sets of samples from the same site at different times

options.label: D
options.text: Collect 3 sets of samples from 3 different sites at different times

questions.answerText: Collect 3 sets of samples from 3 different sites at different times
questions.solutionHtml:
Collect 3 sets of samples from 3 different sites at different times
  • The patient is suspected to have infective endocarditis.
  • The most appropriate sampling method for diagnosis is to collect 3 sets of blood samples – 20ml each – 24 hours apart.
